Prevention: Strict adherence to the cotton close season (1st
This is in place to combat this pest.
Avoid growing crops from same family, e.g. okra and sorrel, nearby.
Prior to the start of the cotton close season swipe, plough and harrow field so as to bury any pests.
Use of trap counts information from the growing season and close season to determine if
PBW will be a serious pest in your area.
Wild cotton and volunteer plants should be destroyed during close season as these will harbour the pest.
Monitoring: Eggs – small, laid singly or in small groups, white when first laid but then turn orange, mostly found on squares and bolls.
Hatch in about three to four days.
Larvae – white with a brown head when they hatch.
They have four stages of growth (instars) and begin to turn pink in the fourth instar.
Use of pheromone traps to attract male adults (1 for 5 acres).
Look for fallen. squares, floral buds or immature bolls.
Direct Control: L pheromone twisted ties at a rate of 100-200 ropes/acre
However, delay use of insecticides as long as possible to allow build-up of natural enemies.
If more than 7 adults are trapped in one night, action is required.
Alternatively if 5% of bolls are attacked, take action.
